page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.24xlarge is an ARM-based general-purpose instance driven by 96 dedicated AWS Neoverse-V2 physical cores based on the ARMv9 architecture, clocked at 2.8 GHz. Featuring dedicated execution without simultaneous multithreading, each virtual CPU maps directly to a physical core. The platform supplies 384.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor, incorporates a 300 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated GPUs, and includes no local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional multi-threaded compute and throughput capabilities. The instance secures top-tier classifications in multi-core stress-ng (163,463.15) and Geekbench multi-core (25,937.0), with marked strengths in parallelized tasks like Clang software compilation (93,246.0) and ray tracing (102,538.0). Memory subsystems deliver top-tier bandwidth, exceeding 481 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads and 240 GB/sec in uncached writes. Network and concurrency benchmarks also register top-tier performance, highlighted by 195.57 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 120.85 GB/sec in static web serving. In contrast, single-core metrics across Geekbench (1,892.0) and stress-ng (1,706.09) settle within the average range.

The lack of bundled local storage is offset by high-capacity 300 Gbps network connectivity, which allows for substantial remote storage throughput. By eliminating thread contention via dedicated physical cores, the instance provides strong resource efficiency for horizontally scaled, compute-heavy concurrent tasks. AWS m8gn.24xlarge is best positioned for large-scale distributed caching, enterprise-grade Redis deployments, high-concurrency web serving, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and containerized microservice clusters.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gn.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance built on the ARMv9 architecture using 96 dedicated AWS Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 2.8 GHz. Designed without simultaneous multithreading, each virtual CPU corresponds to a dedicated physical core. The system provides 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB per core allocation, alongside a high-throughput 300 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, relying on external EBS volumes for persistent state. Benchmark metrics reveal strong multi-core scaling, with top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench software compilation, memory write bandwidth, and static web serving, while single-core performance remains mid-tier. This balance of massive core density, wide memory bandwidth, and high network throughput provides strong resource efficiency for large-scale container clusters, multi-threaded CI/CD builds, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, and high-concurrency enterprise backend applications.
